children: gained 5.2% in Wednesday's trading as J.P. Morgan assumed coverage and upgraded to Overweight from Neutral with a $6 price target, reflecting higher lithium price assumptions that should lift long-term earnings power from 2029 onward and drive a materially higher net asset value.

"Our more constructive stance reflects LCE pricing holding above $20/kg since mid-February (currently $22.3/kg) and our expectation for a market deficit through the end of the decade as Western greenfield supply remains sidelined amid slower capital deployment and longer ramp profiles for previously curtailed assets, dynamics we do not believe fully offset strengthening demand from ESS and EVs," JPM's Rock Hoffman wrote.
Furthermore, the analyst said recent updates boost his confidence in the execution of Thacker Pass, the company's lithium mining and processing project in Nevada.

"With Thacker Pass detailed engineering more than 95% complete and procurement more than 80% complete, alongside continued U.S. policy focus on securing domestic critical mineral supply, we see build time, cost visibility, and customer demand as increasingly de-risked, supporting valuation normalization toward that of a producing asset as the project advances," Hoffman said.

title: Lithium Americas jumps as J.P. Morgan upgrades on improved long-term lithium outlook
